title: In 1969, Engineers Switched Off Niagara Falls for 5 Months

scenes.text: In 1969, engineers switched off Niagara Falls.
The Army Corps of Engineers dumped 28,000 tons of rock into the river. A 600 foot dam above the American Falls.
In three days, one of the most famous waterfalls on Earth shrank to a trickle.
Rockfalls had piled boulders ten storeys high at the bottom, cutting the falls to half their height.
Geologists cleared the loose rock, fitted sensors, and left the boulders alone.
Five months later they tore the dam down. Within a day, Niagara was roaring again.

description:
In June 1969, the US Army Corps of Engineers dumped about 28,000 tons of rock into the Niagara River to build a 600 foot cofferdam, and the American Falls dried to a trickle for five months.
Rockfalls had piled boulders ten storeys high at the base, halving the falls' height. Geologists stabilised the cliff and fitted sensors but left the rock in place; the dam was removed on November 25 and the water returned within a day.
Would you have gone to see Niagara Falls dry?
first_comment: In 1848 the falls stopped by themselves for about 30 hours when an ice jam blocked the river, and people walked out onto the riverbed. Which would you rather see: the falls roaring or the falls dry?
